chunks: From him, from Ibn Faddal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), or he informed me about the one who asked him, regarding a man who comes to his wife in that place (the anus) while a group of people are in the house. He said to me, and raised his voice, saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever imposes on his slave what he cannot bear, let him free him.' Then he looked at the faces of the Ahl al-Bayt, then inclined towards me and said: 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْبَيْتِ: the Ahl al-Bayt (the family of the Prophet)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it (permissible)
key_terms.يَأْتِي الْمَرْأَةَ: comes to the wife (referring to sexual intercourse)

ai.seo_question: Is anal intercourse permissible in Shia Islam according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the permissibility of anal intercourse with one's wife, a point of scholarly discussion regarding whether it is merely permissible (*mubah*) or recommended (*mustahabb*). The narrative structure highlights the Imam’s deliberate pause to observe the reactions of the Ahl al-Bayt, signaling the significance of the ruling before declaring 'no harm' (*la ba'sa bihi*). This incident is frequently cited in Shia fiqh to establish the permissibility of the act within the marital bond, distinguishing it from prohibitions found in other traditions.
